_An Unofficial History of the Wizard's Court, Volume 1_   
  
by A. Hawthorn (signed 716 AE)  
  
Foreword, I suppose.  
  
Isgarren tasked me with writing out a complete history of the Wizard's Court by hand. I'm pretty sure this is torture for asking his age during the reading of my latest scroll translation—had that smug little grin on his face again. Forever kicking myself over not accepting Waiting Sorrow's invitation to join her at the Bastion of the Celestial.   
  
I've been sitting in the library for hours. Basic records, books of spells. Anything and everything you need to know about the potency of poisonous flora found in the Underworld. Things I ALREADY know, having served as the leading archivist for two decades. Nothing personal about Akeem, or Vass. Nothing about Isgarren's time before the court was founded.  
  
I suppose that raises the conundrum. I've been a leading archivist on the bastion for twenty-three years, and my knowledge is embarrassingly limited compared to his. Isgarren's ramblings about the prior cycle have always given me pause, but more recently, they have drawn my attention to the fact that he's kept that knowledge just out of reach from all but Mabon, maybe Sorrow. How isn't there a history of the court already?

strings.en:
Writing this down in case something happens to me.  
  
Skulli got word about these ruins outside this old abandoned city. No one had reported it before, even though we sailed through these parts once or twice. I don't remember the name now—Skulli was always the smart one. The important thing is...he says there's untold riches there. Just waiting for someone to discover it. Pirates always get excited over ruins.  
  
First, I told him he's full of it, but he was insistent. And he kept going on and on...something about the look in his eye told me he weren't lying. So I gathered the rest of the crew. We made it down here, but I'm all that's left.  
  
There's all these crazy-looking critters roaming about, looking infected or something! One of those took out Clance. And the spiders...ugh! They scared off Ajai, the coward. Don't know where she went.  
  
We found an abandoned camp—probably not abandoned for all that long. Murph said that the clothes looked like White Mantle. Not my business to judge.  
  
Me and Murph, we tried to get out, but something kept pushing us back in. We found some sorta sealed door that looked like it was tied to some weird glowing statues nearby. Some kinda puzzle? Murph went off to look for clues, but he's been gone a long time. Got a bad feeling...  
  
I keep hearing rustling from above, like something's up in th—

For nearly one hundred years following our flight, we lived the lives we had so often dreamed of, free of persecution by the Flame Legion.

As we traveled south and built the society that would one day be called Olmakhan, we were forced to question many of the age-old norms of charr society. We were starting from nothing, and in a foreign, hostile landscape no less. To survive, there would need to be changes.

There would be no sense of superiority over the land. This was the core dictum of the Olmakhan: peace with nature, so that we might thrive beyond mere survival. Only a thorough understanding of our new environment would allow us to remain here, to build villages, farms, and families.

For nearly one hundred years we strove to achieve this ideal. It was then that nature sent us our first true test of resolve: a cataclysm beyond our northern horizon that shook the seafloor, and the Great Flood that made an archipelago of our new homeland.

In single moment, it seemed that all we'd built was lost. Many of our tribe were claimed by nature that day, but none truly despaired. Our culture had been forged in struggle and tempered by hardship, and our commitment to our Olmakhan family shone like steel in the sun once the waters receded. We rebuilt, and we thrived again.

Recent times have brought hints of a troubled, larger world that threatens to wash away our peace. First came the spread of the cruel little ones across these islands, with their stone and crystal wonders that defy gravity and their unnatural creations brought to life with unfamiliar magics. 

Then came the great iron sky-whale, breathing smog and flame as it crashed into the soft sands of our shoreline. Its metal shell protects our elder council as they meet to plan our response to the threat of the Inquest, and we've begun to fortify our structures with its iron skeleton.

Nature has presented us with new challenges, and if we must adapt to survive these trials, we will.

As the storm raged outside, the Claw looked over his people. Bearkin were huddled together for warmth—their bellies rumbled, and worry laced their eyes. But the wind was too fierce and the falling snow too thick to hunt. He looked at shivering cubs and made his choice: the Claw would lead them south, away from danger. He could wait for her no longer.

Professor Drugga sent us to scout the forest west of our new operations base. It was a largely uneventful assignment—we didn't want to venture too far without backup—but when we started making our way back, my scanner would not cease beeping. It kept warning us about spikes of unidentified energies nearby, but we couldn't see, hear, or smell anything. I assumed the damn thing malfunctioned...until Yipp took a step forward and vanished. All that was left behind was a glittering ripple in the air and a single drawn-out scream. Kaysi and I lingered there for a while, mostly due to the shock, but we also observed numerous local creatures enter the same area and disappear as well. 
  
Right before we headed back to base, Yipp emerged from the thicket drenched in sweat. He explained that after vanishing, he reappeared about a mile south of our location—spit out of a rift that opened up in the sky. We marked the location and headed right back to base to inform Drugga. She immediately escalated our findings to the director himself, who ordered us to build a small containment facility around the spot.  
  
I wonder if we can use this to our advantage...

Dear Isla, Antonie, and Zora,

Hello again, my loves. I feel as though I see you around every corner and behind every rock. Your voices giggle at the edge of my consciousness, just out of range. If only I could reach out and... But you pull away every time I get close.

You all are the warmth of the sun on my skin and the icy shock of deep water, reminding me of what I once had and cruelly taunting me about what I've lost. Nothing ever changes on this island; all three of you still shimmer in my mind as you did on the last day I saw you. I cannot decide which is worse—that you will be forever frozen to me as you were then, or that you will change and grow old while I remain here, staring into the ceaseless waves.

Watch over them for me, Isla.

Yours forever, wherever the Mists take me,
Nathaniel
